books.section: Topic 5.8 Military Conflict in the Civil War
Unit 5: Toward the Civil War and Reconstruction (1844–1877)

primary_sources: Abraham Lincoln, letter to Horace Greeley (August 22, 1862)

stimulus.source_note: Abraham Lincoln, letter to Horace Greeley, August 22, 1862. Public domain; quoted as printed in Princeton Review, Chapter 9 supplement. “. . .” marks omitted text.
stimulus.text:
“If I could save the Union without freeing any slave I would do it, and if I could save it by freeing all the slaves I would do it; and if I could save it by freeing some and leaving others alone I would also do that. What I do about slavery, and the colored race, I do because I believe it helps to save the Union. . . .”

—Abraham Lincoln, letter to Horace Greeley, August 22, 1862

source: original; stimulus as noted in stimulus.source_note
stem: Within a month of this letter, Antietam gave Lincoln the victory he needed to issue the Emancipation Proclamation. The letter and the proclamation together best show that Lincoln’s war aims

options.misconception: In the letter Lincoln treats emancipation as a means; the proclamation makes it a war aim, which is a change.
Lincoln answered Greeley, but he set his own timing and terms.

options.text: abandoned the Union in favor of abolition alone.
options.misconception: Lincoln never abandoned the Union; he added emancipation to it.

options.text: shifted from Union alone to Union and ending slavery.

rationales.A: In the letter Lincoln treats emancipation as a means; the proclamation makes it a war aim, which is a change.
rationales.B: Lincoln answered Greeley, but he set his own timing and terms.
rationales.C: Lincoln never abandoned the Union; he added emancipation to it.
rationales.D: Background from the books: the proclamation changed the nature of the war for the North.
rationales.general:
1. In August 1862 Lincoln says he will do about slavery whatever saves the Union.
2. In September Antietam gives him a victory, and he acts on the emancipation half of that sentence.
3. Background from the books: from January 1863 the war has two stated purposes, not one.
4. Background from the books: the proclamation changed the nature of the war for the North.
Remember: put the letter and the proclamation side by side: the second adds what the first weighed.
